newsitem.title: USA: Edison Intl Calif. nuke restart delayed.
newsitem.headline: Edison Intl Calif. nuke restart delayed.

text.p: Edison International's 1,070 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear power unit will not restart this Friday as previously scheduled, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Tuesday in its plant status report.
Repairs to a leak are expected to take approximately five days. The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., is now scheduled to restart around March 13, according to the NRC report.
Restart of the unit, which has been shut for maintenance and refueling since Nov 30, was delayed for the first time in early February to repair generator tubes.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, is operating at full power.
The plant is majority owned and operated by Edison, while Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co owns 20 percent and the cities of Anaheim and Riverside own the remaining five percent.
